Subject: Re: Initial: acceptance criteria for Pilot POC

Jordan — thanks, sending a focused draft below and attaching a spreadsheet with the scoring matrix. Quick notes up top:

- We broke acceptance into three buckets: Reliability (uptime/errors), Performance (latency/throughput), and Quality (concordance and safety samples).
- For accept/fail decisions we propose a two-stage gate: smoke verification at week 1, then a proof-of-outcome gate at the end of week 4.
- Fail-fast triggers are designed to avoid wasted ops time (auto-escalate to our SRE and pause traffic if P95 latency > 1.5x target for 3 consecutive hours).

Draft MAP excerpt (summary):

Reliability- Target uptime: >= 99.5% over the 4-week window- Accept if daily error rate < 0.5% (5xx or model timeouts)- Fail-fast: any sustained spike > 2% for 2+ hours => immediate remediation window, then pause test traffic if unresolved

Performance- Latency target (p95): <= 350ms for typical clinical prompt set- Throughput: sustain 8 RPS with 95% of requests meeting p95 latency- Fail-fast: p95 > 700ms for 3 consecutive hours => trigger autoscaling review and temporary throttling

Quality / Concordance- Metric: human-reviewed concordance on 200 random samples (mix of edge cases)- Acceptance: >= 92% concordant with baseline clinical decisions and no safety-critical mispredictions- Escalation: any single safety-critical misprediction => immediate pause and root-cause review

Operational Acceptance Tests (examples):
1) Smoke: endpoint sanity, model routing verification, KV cache validates token reuse (week 1)
2) Stability: 3-day continuous run at target RPS with sampling checks (week 2-3)
3) Outcome: 200-sample concordance review + latency and error windows (end week 4)

I've attached novamed-map-v1.xlsx with the scoring weights and a checklist you can attach to the SOW. Karthik / Marissa — please scan for anything we should hard-fail in the contract language.

Thanks,
Monica
Monica Patel
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 7 Aug 2026 12:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft: evaluation acceptance scoring & fail-fast procedures

Quick internal: I read the draft — looks solid. A couple of legal/ops notes to flag before we share broadly:

- Suggest we tighten the rollback wording: instead of "pause test traffic" use "pause production-like traffic to the trial environment" and require a documented remediation plan within 24 hours. That prevents ambiguous interpretation in the SOW.
- Add explicit data retention confirmation: trial logs kept for 90 days and access controlled under our SOC2 process. Novamed asked about audit logs during the demo.
- For latency thresholds, propose a conditional fallback: if p95 breaches between 350-700ms but error rate remains low, we recommend emergency scaling rather than immediate pause. Full pause reserved for >700ms or >2% error rate.

I'll draft suggested contractual language and drop into the spreadsheet as a redline.

Karthik
VP, Solutions
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

+1 to Karthik's comments. Also suggest we make the concordance sample selection reproducible: define stratified sampling (by encounter type and prompt length) and seed the sample so both teams can verify.

I'll add a sample sampling script and a short blurb about evidence owners for each test (who signs off on the 200-sample review).

Marissa
